title: improv·artist · tender (Felix Gonzalez-Torres)
mutation_directive: improv artist: tender via Felix Gonzalez-Torres

improv_extras.practice: candy spills, light strings, paired clocks; intimacy as sculpture

v1.feedback: The Gonzalez-Torres light-string concept lands clearly — differential growth producing catenary drapes with warm incandescent bulb particles is a legible, tender translation of the source artist. The palette (amber → warm white) is restrained and appropriate, and additive blending sells the glow. Two improvements: the fog density and depth falloff dim the rear strands too aggressively, flattening what should read as a spatial installation — reduce uFogDensity to ~0.02 and widen the camera FOV slightly so the full drape reads as a hung object in a room. Second, the growth currently stays mostly planar in XZ with only gravity on Y; adding a second or third strand offset in Z (parallel strings at different depths, like the actual installations) would strengthen the reference and give the 3D orbit more to reveal.

v2.feedback: The Gonzalez-Torres light-string concept lands clearly — multiple catenary curves with warm amber bulb points read as draped domestic light strings within 2 seconds, and the differential-growth subdivision adds organic texture without overwhelming the form. The palette is restrained and appropriate (amber/copper/warm white). Two things to tighten: the fog density and camera distance leave the lower strands fading into murk — pull the camera closer or reduce fog so all five strands read with equal presence; and the bulb flicker is too subtle at 8% amplitude — push it to 15-20% with slightly staggered frequencies per strand to evoke the vulnerability of actual incandescent bulbs, which is where the 'tender' keyword should really live. The wire particles between bulbs could be thinner (smaller point size) to increase the contrast between dark cord and glowing bulb, sharpening the installation silhouette.
